discovery: Conception and construction of the ATLAS and CMS detectors at the LHC, leading to the experimental discovery of the Higgs boson
motivation: The 2013 Prize honoured the theoretical prediction of the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism, but the observation of the Higgs boson in 2012 was an experimental triumph that has not been recognised. Michel Della Negra and Tejinder Virdee conceived the Compact Muon Solenoid, with its high-field solenoid and high-resolution crystal calorimeter designed specifically to see H to two photons. Peter Jenni led the founding and design of ATLAS through its construction. Their detector concepts, sustained over two decades of R&D, made it possible to pick out a rare signal amid billions of proton collisions per second, and they delivered two independent, mutually confirming observations. These instruments have since measured the Higgs couplings, set the frontier for searches beyond the Standard Model, and pioneered trigger, timing and data methods now used across physics. Recognising them would honour the instrumentation behind the discovery that completed the Standard Model.
